results.description: Yes, primarily at Korala. Rasuwagadhi and Tatopani (the usual main routes for Chinese EVs) have been closed or heavily disrupted by floods and landslides since late August. Trade was diverted there, so Korala cleared 6,501 EVs (mid-July–Oct 30). National Q1 total was ~6,636 EVs overall; China supplied most, nearly all via Korala. Limited activity has resumed at Rasuwagadhi but remains minor.

results.title: Trade volume with China has increased overall, driven by rising imports.
results.description:
Trade volume with China has increased overall, driven by rising imports.

Nepal imported Rs 425 bn from China in FY 2025/26, up 24.7% from Rs 341 bn the prior year. Exports stayed tiny at ~Rs 1.9 bn (often declining). 

Current FY 2026/27 shows continued growth; Mustang alone cleared Rs 26 bn in imports (incl. 6501 EVs) in 3.5 months—already far above its full prior-year total—amid border shifts.

results.title: Two Floods, Two Outcomes Nepal's August 26, 2026 flood in the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli river system killed about 1,453 people.
results.description:
Two Floods, Two Outcomes

Nepal's August 26, 2026 flood in the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli river system killed about 1,453 people. It struck Timure, Rasuwagadhi and Syabrubesiin Rasuwa first around 9 am, in broad daylight, without warning since there were no automated sirens. The failure to instal warning system proved fatal in Nepal. 

Bhutan's October 29 Shintaphu GLOF, in the Mo Chhu–Punatsangchhu / Sankosh basin struck at night. Yet within 10–15 minutes, people were alerted since lake sensors triggered sirens across the valley. Gasa Tshachu was evacuated before destruction.

Daylight did not save Nepal; darkness did not doom Bhutan. Early warning, not time of day, decided who lived.#Bhutanfloods
